text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: High 5xx spike + streaming disconnect surge observed from gateway cluster eu-west-2. Primary symptom: chunked-response truncation and client-side cancels around 15-30s. Pager: Lina Gomez. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-3123457890 :rotating_light:

Lina Gomez: Paging oncall. Customers reporting half-finished streams that never finish. Also getting reports of timeouts proxied at the edge.

oncall-bot: Auto-assign -> Ben O'Neill. If you're unavailable react with :wave:.

Ben O'Neill: I'm up. Checking ingress/gateway metrics and recent deploys. Which regions are impacted?

Lina Gomez: eu-west-2 primarily, small blip in us-east-1. Streaming endpoints (/v1/stream, /ws/proxy) show highest error rates. Paged APIs show a transient 504 tail.

Harpreet Singh: I pulled nginx/gateway logs and saw repeated "client prematurely closed connection" and "invalid chunked terminator" errors. Sample tail:

Harpreet Singh: ```
2026-03-15T13:01:12Z gw-eu-02 proxy: invalid chunked terminator from upstream 10.3.4.12:5342
2026-03-15T13:01:13Z gw-eu-02 proxy: client closed connection (RST) after 17s
2026-03-15T13:01:14Z runtime-pod-9 model: slow token gen: 2.8s per token under seq_len>800
2026-03-15T13:01:15Z gw-eu-02 kernel: tcp_retrans_out increased by 300 in 30s
```

eng-runtime-bot: Collected pprof heap/cpu for runtime pods runtime-pod-{7,8,9}. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/prof/3123457890. Noted elevated mutex wait on kv-cache and occasional GC pauses ~120ms.

Ben O'Neill: Quick mitigation plan options: A) shift traffic off gw-eu-02 to other gateways B) enable stream->paged downgrade per-tenant C) bump gateway read timeout to 75s D) scale runtime shards up by 1. Prioritizing low-risk moves first.

Lina Gomez: Start with B and A. Downgrading affected tenants keeps requests served although interactive UX degrades. Move traffic off gw-eu-02 after we start downgrades. Also notify CS for impacted customers.

Harpreet Singh: We have a per-tenant routing override: admin toggle streaming_downgrade=true. I'll flip it for tenant IDs: acme-corp, medsys, retail-one with a 2% canary then ramp.

Ben O'Neill: I'll cordon gw-eu-02 and do a soft weight ramp down in the LB. Command (k8s): `kubectl label node gw-eu-02 maintenance=true && lbctl weight gw-eu-02 70%` then 50%->0 over 120s.

Lina Gomez: CS notified. Draft note: "We're seeing intermittent streaming disconnects; temporarily routing affected traffic to a paged fallback and rebalancing gateways while we investigate a kernel-level retransmit spike."

Harpreet Singh: Canary started for acme-corp at 2%. Initial telemetry: streaming errors for that tenant down ~78%, overall stream 5xx down ~30% in eu-west-2.

eng-runtime-bot: Runtime traces show lock contention on kv_cache::alloc path and bursts of batch formation timeouts when sequence length distribution spikes >800. Also saw one pod OOMKilled 3h ago (runtime-pod-6).

Ben O'Neill: After starting soft drain, tcp retransmit counters on gw-eu-02 dropped significantly. Still seeing occasional 502s from runtime proxies.

Lina Gomez: Can we temporarily reduce worker concurrency on runtime to reduce tail latency? Also consider eviction TTL on KV cache to avoid heavy allocations. Harpreet, can you test safe knobs?

Harpreet Singh: Propose KV_CACHE_TTL=240 (was 1800), WORKER_CONCURRENCY=6 (was 10) for streaming workers on two non-critical shards first. Rolling to one shard now: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime-pod-9 KV_CACHE_TTL=240 WORKER_CONCURRENCY=6`

Ben O'Neill: Applied soft drain and reroute. Observed cluster streaming disconnects down ~55% and 5xx trending toward baseline.

Lina Gomez: Are there any related deploys in the last 6 hours? I want to rule out recent changelists.

Harpreet Singh: No runtime deploys in last 8h. Network kernel updates on gw-eu-02 were rolled 14h ago but didn't correlate earlier. Could be a workload pattern causing cache churn.

eng-runtime-bot: Heap profile link attached to postmortem. GC pause distribution shifted right for pods with sequence_len>800. KV cache eviction rates spiked at incident start.

Ben O'Neill: Next steps: finish tenant downgrade rollout (acme-corp, medsys, retail-one), keep gw-eu-02 out of LB for 30m, monitor. If errors remain, we will scale runtime workload by +1 replica and attempt to toggle streaming chunking mode to smaller chunks.

Lina Gomez: Agree. Assigning tasks and ETA:
- Lina: coordinate customer comms & Slack ASAs (ETA 45m)
- Ben: gateway drain + LB adjustments + post-incident kernel tuning notes (ETA 2h)
- Harpreet: runtime env knob tests, memory/pprof analysis, and patch recommendation (ETA 4h)
- eng-runtime-bot: attach traces and heapdumps to postmortem doc (ongoing)

Harpreet Singh: Rolling the tenant flag to 100% for acme-corp now. medsys and retail-one queued after 10m of stability.

Ben O'Neill: All tenant downgrades complete. Observed sustained reduction in streaming 5xx to within SLO for eu-west-2. Paged API 504s are back to normal.

Lina Gomez: Leaving this thread open as SRO. If anything regresses ping @Ben and escalate to on-call SRE. We'll create a full postmortem with timeline, kernel retransmit telemetry, kv-cache contention, and the tenant downgrade mitigation.

SRE Pager: Incident acknowledged. Postmortem stub created: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-3123457890

Ben O'Neill: Quick note for postmortem: include exact tcp retransmit deltas per host, pprof evidence of kv alloc lock, and the per-tenant flag rollback steps.

Harpreet Singh: I'll attach heap and cpu profiles in the doc and include safe rollout plan for KV cache fix.

Lina Gomez: Thank you all. Handoff to Ben for next 30m monitoring while I prepare customer update. Will reconvene with summary in this thread when done. :white_check_mark:
